title: Customer identities
brief: Customers are told apart by identity, not by name. Two customers who share a name are still two customers.
instructions: Return every customer identity with its name. Rows sharing a name stay separate; I will not merge people for you.
Return only the declared columns, in their declared order and exact SQL types, and follow the stated ordering contract. NULL placement is declared, not assumed.
starterExplanation: The starter reads customer_id, customer_name and email out of customers. It runs. It does not answer the question.

hints.text: Projection alone keeps identities apart. Nothing here needs grouping.
Read the identity and the name straight out of the customers table.
Grading includes a variant where three customers share the name Ari. All three must survive.

dataClaims.sql: SELECT count(*)::VARCHAR FROM customers WHERE customer_name = 'Ari'
dataClaims.claim: hints[2]: three customers share the name Ari in the boundary variant
